text.tspan: C2-E17 · Derived probability under a prescribed Poisson rate
A and B have different rates and durations but the same
integral, so they end at the same activation probability.
C has the high rate but too little time.
Rate alone does not decide activation: the product of rate and time spent in the activating state does. J(T, p) must be supplied
Independent Poisson events; survival S = exp(−∫Λ dt) (Eq. C2-E17). Rates are illustrative.
